blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-privacy-1 (Account deletion keeps the member's personal data in the users row) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
_conn.execute(
    "UPDATE users SET deleted_at = datetime('now'), password_hash = NULL WHERE id = ?",
    (user_id,),
)
findings.recommendation: The proposal promises that the button "erases the member's personal data", and the member exercises the right to erasure (GDPR Art. 17), but delete_account only sets deleted_at and clears password_hash: email, display_name, phone and postal_address (app/schema.sql) stay in the users row indefinitely. Scenario: a member clicks "Delete my account"; afterwards SELECT email, display_name, phone, postal_address FROM users WHERE id = ? still returns all four values. The orders kept for accounting reference users.id, so they stay linked to the member's identity, contrary to "kept for accounting, without personal data". Overwrite the personal columns in the same UPDATE — display_name, phone and postal_address to NULL or a placeholder, email to a unique non-personal value such as 'deleted-<id>' (the column is NOT NULL UNIQUE, which also frees the address for a later sign-up) — and add a test asserting those columns no longer hold the member's data after delete_account.
findings.title: Account deletion keeps the member's personal data in the users row

findings.recommendation: analytics_id is added by this change but nothing in the change uses it, and the plan states no purpose for it (GDPR Art. 5(1)(b)-(c)). It is a pseudonym, not an anonymous value: with one global salt it is a deterministic function of users.id, which the change keeps (the users row and the orders that reference it), so analytics events carrying it stay re-identifiable after the member deletes the account, and delete_account does nothing to the analytics data. The analytics pipeline is not visible here, hence confidence low. Either drop analytics_id from this change, or state its purpose and make erasure reach it — delete or detach the member's events, or derive the id from a per-user random value that delete_account destroys.
findings.title: The new analytics id stays linkable after the account is deleted

findings.evidence:
def delete_account(user_id: int) -> None:
    """Deletes the member's account; their orders are kept for accounting."""
findings.recommendation: Neither the plan nor the code says how long a deleted users row is kept, nor how the erasure reaches backups of members.db (GDPR Art. 5(1)(e), Art. 17). The backup setup is not visible here, hence confidence low. State the retention of soft-deleted rows (or purge them after a set delay) and how backups expire or are scrubbed, so that an erased member's data does not survive a restore.
findings.title: Erasure from backups and the retention of deleted rows are not defined
